All reassurance sits BELOW the form: COD and inspection promises in the 4-card 'Why ZAVA' grid (block 8) and a gold 'inspect the product on receipt' pill + FAQ answers (block 9). Above the form, persuasion is purely product-feature imagery.
analyses.structuralSignature: The persuasion zone is five full-bleed pre-rendered infographic PNGs (Amazon-A+ style) with zero HTML text, prices, or CTAs; every interactive element — bundles, variant pickers, pricing, live totals — is concentrated in one dense form block, with reassurance (why-us cards + dark FAQ footer) placed after the form instead of before it. Distinctive moves: a conditional sticky CTA is the only order path from the image zone; the FAQ delivery-time answer is data-bound to the wilaya dropdown in the form; and the post-submit success state is inline markup right below the form.

skeletons.name: poster-funnel-trust-after
skeletons.notes: The pre-form zone is pure product imagery with no price and no inline CTA. The sticky bottom bar is the only order path before the form (IntersectionObserver hides it when the form is visible). Trust content (why-us grid, FAQ with COD and inspect-on-delivery answers) sits AFTER the form. Note: the raw refs put price and CTA only in the form; under the hero-economy law the hero must gain price + CTA + trust chips, so this skeleton keeps its ORDER but not its price-free hero. Counted content blocks: hero, problem-solution, benefits-icons, variant-gallery (or faq), order-form; announcement-bar/sticky-cta are chrome.

skeletons.name: technical-catalog
skeletons.notes: Ultra-short spec pitch: hero holds a price card with embedded trust chips and a full-width anchor CTA; then one annotated-parts infographic plus icon benefit cards; then a 2-3 photo use-case gallery (mapped to unboxing-gallery, the nearest id — these are staged demo photos, not customer photos); then the form as the last content block. Zero social proof, zero urgency mechanics. The header doubles as an announcement bar (delivery-coverage pill).

skeletons.name: offer-metronome
skeletons.notes: A rhythm machine: each support block ends with the same CTA + identical price/gift recap subline (6 repetitions before the form). Urgency attaches to a free GIFT, not stock. A full price-anchor reminder card sits immediately before the form. Hard stop at the form: no footer, no FAQ, no proof. At 8 raw blocks this exceeds the 6-block law; the compliant cut merges stock-urgency into the price-anchor card: hero, benefits-icons, spec-table, price-anchor(+gift urgency), order-form. Fully fact-free — needs no supplied reviews.

skeletons.name: gift-proof-minimal
skeletons.notes: Five content blocks, exactly ONE CTA (the form submit), zero prices outside the form. The hero sells with a numeric social-proof headline plus trust bullets. Main persuasion block is a gift-with-purchase showcase (mapped to cross-sell, the nearest id). Proof is one designed collage image placed directly BEFORE the form. Under the hero-economy law the hero must gain price + CTA; under the spine law a sticky-cta must be added (the ref has none). photo-reviews REQUIRES supplied review assets — fact-free fallback: swap to faq or guarantee-seal.

skeletons.name: lean-demo-funnel
skeletons.notes: Lean linear funnel. The sticky element is a TOP header with a small anchor pill CTA (no bottom bar). The full price ladder lives in the hero subheadline prose. Zero social proof — its slot is filled by a 3-photo captioned demo gallery placed right before the form (mapped to unboxing-gallery). Bundles exist only as radio cards inside the form. This ref is fully law-compatible as-is.

skeletons.name: editorial-lookbook
skeletons.notes: Numbered-chapter lookbook: the variant set is shown twice (selectable gallery, then interactive dark demo — the second pass mapped to before-after as nearest interactive-visual id) and both feed the variant radio in the terminal form. The raw ref has NO price, NO proof, NO sticky bar and its hero CTA points at the gallery, which violates hero-economy and spine laws. Usable only as an adapted archetype for variant-rich products: hero (with law-mandated price/CTA/chips), variant-gallery, one more visual beat, form, plus mandatory sticky-cta.

risks: Fact-gated blocks: the dice can pick photo-reviews, video-testimonial, whatsapp-proof, press-badges, or variant-gallery when the brief supplies no such assets. The sampler must gate these options on brief facts BEFORE the roll (filter, then renormalize weights) — a post-roll fallback that silently swaps blocks makes the recipe and the rendered page disagree.

Law collisions inside proven refs: 3 of 7 refs (137, 13g, 13h) have price-free, CTA-free heroes and glowme has no price at all — these exact patterns violate the hero-economy law. If the skeleton generator copies ref heroes verbatim, it ships illegal pages; the archetypes must inherit ORDER only, with the mandatory hero payload injected.

Correlated dice producing incoherent pages: the sticky-only CTA cadence only makes sense with the poster-funnel skeleton; the metronome cadence assumes text-based support blocks with recap sublines; a top-pill sticky-cta plus a bottom bar doubles the chrome. The sampler needs pairing constraints (cadence and tail conditioned on skeleton) or the whole-skeleton lever should absorb them.

Form-too-early / trust-after-form risk: the mid-page-form + trust-after pattern (137/13g) is proven only for visually rich, branded products with polished poster imagery. Rolled onto a text-heavy generic product, the buyer hits the form with weak persuasion and the post-form FAQ is never read. Weight this skeleton down when the brief has few images.

Block-count accounting ambiguity: whether announcement-bar, sticky-cta, and trust-footer count toward the 4-6 law changes every skeleton's legality (13d is 8 raw blocks). The recipe must fix one convention (chrome excluded; hero + supports + order-form counted) and the validator must enforce it, or dice output will oscillate between legal and illegal.

Collision with the chat brain's SECTIONS list: the dice emit vocabulary ids, but several observed blocks have no exact id (use-case photo gallery, free-gift showcase, brand manifesto, feature posters) and were mapped to nearest ids (unboxing-gallery, cross-sell, before-after). If the chat brain's SECTIONS list or editor uses different ids or does not know these blocks, post-build edits and regenerations will desync. Freeze one shared id registry.

Bundle-offers as a standalone block is UNPROVEN: all 7 refs put bundles inside the form. If the sampler can roll a standalone bundle-offers block (as in today's converged skeleton), it leaves the evidence base; prefer the in-form radio-card presentation.

Determinism and edit stability: without a persisted seed per project, a rebuild rerolls the structure and destroys the user's mental map and any manual edits. Store the rolled recipe with the project and reroll only on explicit request.

Ref quirks that must NOT become levers: 13b's hidden price drop in the submit label (2900 vs advertised 3500) is a dark pattern; 13i's mismatch between the highlighted tier and the pre-checked tier is likely a bug; 137/13g's variant-gallery image failed to load in both captures (unverified block). Copying these degrades trust or ships broken sections.

Baked-image persuasion zones (137/13g posters) are not generatable without supplied designed assets; if the poster-funnel skeleton rolls for a brief with plain photos, the renderer must fall back to native HTML sections or the page loses its entire persuasion mechanism.

Small sample size: 7 refs, 2 of them near-duplicates (137/13g) and 1 not a real shop (glowme). Effective evidence is ~5 archetypes; weights are priors, not measurements. Instrument conversion per rolled recipe and re-weight from live data.
